description.narrative: The objective of the Supporting Egypt Education Reform Project is to improve teaching and learning conditions in public schools. There are five components to the project, the first component being improved early childhood education. The component aims to expand access to quality early childhood education (ECE) in Egypt, through two subcomponents. Increased access to KG, and Improved quality of KG education. The second component is the effective teachers and education leaders. The component aims to improve the pre-tertiary education effectiveness of teachers, education leaders, and supervisors through two subcomponents: improved quality of continuous professional development (CPD) system; and expanded CPD opportunities. The third component is the comprehensive assessment reform for improved student learning. The component has the following four subcomponents: reforming the examination system in upper secondary education, introducing a grade 4 national assessment, transforming the grade 9 examination, and restructuring the NCEEE. The fourth component is the enhancing education service delivery through connected systems. This cross-cutting component will support the government's commitment to invest in new education technology infrastructure and services. Investments in new education technology infrastructure will be funded by the Borrower. Finally, the fifth component is the project management, communication, and monitoring and evaluation.
The project development objective (PDO) is to improve teaching and learning conditions in public schools.

title.narrative: Grievances resolved within the stipulated service standards for response times

comment.narrative: Extracting project-level complaints received at the Ministry level remains challenging and facing cumulative delays. However, MOETE seeks support in establishing a nation-wide functioning GRM system. In Sep 2025, the Ministry submitted a proposal to recruit a technology firm to develop, implement, and maintain a unified GRM system. MOETE and WB teams agreed on launching the recruitment process for hardwares and software required to enhance the GRM system by Jan 2026. In September 2023, a WB consultant drafted the MOETE's GRM situational assessment report and executive summary to support MOETE in understanding its current practices, including the institutional set-up and capacity for the Central Administration of Citizen Services, at the level of the central administration, as well as the educational districts and directorates. The report offered recommendations on the process of registration, sorting, analysis and reporting, creating SOPs.

baseline.value: New CPD framework to guide training modules still being developed

target.value: 25 % of grades 1-6 teachers are trained using the new training modules driven by CPD framework and standards

comment.narrative: CPD- aligned training package “Teaching Essentials” developed and approved in Jan 2025. Training package includes modules focused on: student-centered teaching and learning, classroom management strategies, formative assessment, promoting culture of respect and cooperation in schools, and professional learning communities (PLC), with basic information on utilization of digital technology for education, in addition to examples on climate awareness and gender sensitive behaviors. CPD training delivered to 85,965 G1-6 public school teachers (out of 328,701-26%) Jan-Feb 2025 in 10 governorates. MOETE plans to train additional 30,000 G1-6 teachers, including newly recruited teachers, in another 13 governorates. There has also been a broader focus on teacher training, including training on the new textbooks in 2024/25 which was delivered through online sessions and in-person workshops, with the latter emphasizing the establishment of communities of practice.

actual.value: Achieved - The KG Quality Assurance (QA) system was developed and approved by MOETE Minister in August 2023. The KG QA system was made operational for public and private KGs in February 2024, including: (a) KG QA standards; (b) KG quality assurance system (replacing the system of rewards and sanctions); and (c) monitoring tools with corresponding protocols for assessing KG schools against the QA standards.

title.narrative: 3. Percentage of grades 1-6 teachers of public schools demonstrating effective teaching practice

comment.narrative: 2018/19: 43,500 teachers received new teacher's behavioral program in 14,500 schools. CPD Framework for G1-6 Teachers and Supervisors developed in 2023, finalized and approved by Minister MOETE in January 2025. CPD-driven trainings delivered to 85,965 G1-6 teachers (out of 328,701 – 26%) in Jan-Feb 2025 in 10 governorates. Classroom observation tool (COT) developed under CPD Framework piloted in May 2025. COT being revised to ensure more accurate measurement of performance of teachers with re-administration planned by April 2026, following the next round of teacher trainings scheduled in Jan-Feb 2026.

title.narrative: 3. Percentage of grades 1-6 teachers of public schools demonstrating effective teaching practice

comment.narrative: The CPD framework for G1-6 teachers and supervisors was finalized and approved in January 2025 and included a “Teaching essentials” training for teachers inclusive of various modules. The CPD-driven trainings were delivered to 26% of G1-6 teachers in early 2025 in 10 governorates. Based on the CPD standards, a classroom observation tool was piloted as a means to assess teacher effectiveness in May 2025. Observations results are expected soon. A re-administration of a teacher effectiveness measurement will be scheduled by MOETE during the upcoming academic year 2025/2026 which should serve to provide data for PDO indicator 3.
